## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Sekhiya 66 of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, titled *Veṭhita* ("Wearing a headdress"), is a training rule in the Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic decorum when teaching the Dhamma [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations available on SuttaCentral include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral records extensive parallels across multiple Vinaya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali tradition, direct parallels exist in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sk 66), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Sk 66), the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Sk 66), and both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Parallels in other traditions include Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan texts representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas, as well as the Chinese *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language matches met the threshold score of 10 in the DharmaNexus database [DharmaNexus].
